output.name: Rathun

output.myth: Rathun was a ketch out of the western harbour, and she went to sea the week Tavo came down laughing. The gale took her stern and stove it in like a bad crate. Her crew bailed with their hats, then their boots, then their bare hands, and when the water stood at their knees they sang the old net-song, so that Tavo would hear something he had not heard before. Tavo did not stop, but he grew curious, the way Aun always did. He lifted the ketch on his shoulder, carried her over the Leeward rocks, and set her down in the Upper Sea where the wind runs clean. She is there still. Her sails are full, though her stern is open to the sky, and the wind goes in one side and out the other. Sil sees her on dark nights and waves. The old sailors say that if you hold your breath off the Unflown, you may hear her bailing.
output.verse:
Open stern, full sail,
Tavo set her on the sea.
Wind goes in and out.
